issues.location: finite-union inequality in Dedekind's countable-choice proof
issues.finding: The left side unions A_n repeatedly over i<n, whereas the right side sums the sizes of A_0 through A_{n-1}. The indexed union must use A_i.
issues.proposed_resolution: Use card(union_{i<n} A_i) in the displayed inequality.

issues.finding: The source calls a countable union of countable sets of cardinality beth_1 in a ZF setting. Here beth_1 was introduced as a well-orderable cardinal under Choice, whereas the pertinent example is that the uncountable real line can be such a union without Countable Choice.
issues.proposed_resolution: State the Feferman--Levy example as the uncountable set of reals being a countable union of countable sets, without assigning it a well-orderable beth_1 cardinal in ZF.

translation_treatment: The target fixes the finite-union index and states the Feferman--Levy example using the real line, while preserving the historical attribution and localizing Cohen and Russell page citations. The frozen source remains unchanged.
